subject: Re: Request for temporary latency tolerance & pricing concession
messages:
From: Anna Keller <anna.keller@bluecresthealth.com>
To: camila.reyes@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@bluecresthealth.com
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Temporary latency tolerance & pricing concession request

Hi Camila,

Thanks again for the onboarding support last week. We appreciate Redwood getting the initial model running in our staging cluster. Over the past 48 hours we've observed a higher-than-expected tail latency during peak query windows (p95 spiking to ~2.1s from the usual ~650ms). This has bubbled up to our platform team and product leadership — they're asking for a temporary SLO tolerance while we finish a rollout of client-side batching and a small inference config tweak.

Two asks from our side:
- Can Redwood provisionally accept a p95 latency tolerance of up to 2.5s for an interim period (we're proposing 8 weeks)?
- In exchange, we'd like a 15% unit pricing concession for that period (we're still in pilot and pushing more volume once latency stabilizes).

We can share incident logs and a short runbook describing mitigation steps (attached is a summary). We understand this is non-standard — please let us know what you need from legal/ops to evaluate.

Best,
Anna
Anna Keller
Director, Platform Engineering
Bluecrest Health

Attachment: Bluecrest_Support_Incidents_May.pdf (summary of incidents, 5 pages)
From: camila.reyes@redwood.com <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
To: Anna Keller <anna.keller@bluecresthealth.com>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Temporary latency tolerance & pricing concession request

Hi Anna — thanks for the clear summary and the incident notes, appreciated. We're glad the engine is otherwise behaving and that your team has a mitigation plan.

Short answer: we can consider a short-term SLO adjustment paired with a commercial concession, but this requires a Deal Desk/Exec approval because it changes our default SLA and pricing. I will escalate internally and propose some guardrails to make this safe for both sides:

Proposed guardrails (tentative):
- Duration: 8 weeks maximum, effective once protocol is signed.
- Scope: Applies only to the Bluecrest production route and the specific model variant currently in use.
- Service credit cap: service credit for any qualifying downtime or degraded performance will be limited to 10% of monthly invoice for the interim period (instead of standard SLA scale).
- Observable checkpoints: weekly performance review with a shared dashboard and a mandatory joint runbook update at week 4.
- Reversion: automatic reversion to standard SLOs at the end of the interval unless both parties agree to extend.

I'll loop in Deal Desk (Marissa) and our legal/ops reviewer (Rishi) to get an official decision and a short amendment. Can you confirm you accept the service-credit cap and weekly review cadence? If so, I'll push to get a decision by EOD tomorrow.

Regards,
Camila Reyes
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Marissa / Rishi — forwarding Bluecrest's ask. Summary: Bluecrest is requesting a provisional p95 latency tolerance up to 2.5s for 8 weeks plus a 15% unit pricing concession during the window. They supplied incident notes (attached).

What I propose we consider:
- Approve a 6–8 week temporary latency carveout (I recommend 6 weeks to limit exposure) with a hard service-credit cap of 10% monthly invoice.
- Offer a tiered commercial concession: 10% for first 3 weeks, 5% thereafter (total effective concession averages to ~8% over 6 weeks) — this reduces our revenue exposure vs. a flat 15%.
- Require a joint performance gate at week 3 to either: (a) return to standard SLO, (b) extend for an additional 2 weeks with formal exec sign-off, or (c) trigger escalation.

Why tiered concession? It gives Bluecrest an incentive to remediate quickly and limits Redwood's discount tail risk. Bluecrest needs the predictability for their billing so they're likely to accept a defined window.

Attachments: Bluecrest_Support_Incidents_May.pdf, proposed_guardrails.xlsx

Can you confirm whether Deal Desk can greenlight a tiered concession structure and the 10% service-credit cap? If you approve, I'll propose the language and condition list to the customer and get a signed amendment.

Thanks,
Camila
From: marissa.cole@redwood.com <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: camila.reyes@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 15:32:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FW: Temporary latency tolerance & pricing concession request

Camila — thanks for the clear framing and the proposed mitigations. I've reviewed the incident summary and the proposed guardrails. Deal Desk approves a provisional approach with the following binding conditions:

1) Duration and scope: Approve a 6-week temporary p95 latency carveout (p95 up to 2.5s) for BLUECREST HEALTH, covering the specific production model ID listed in the attachment.
2) Commercial concession: Approve a tiered unit discount as proposed (10% weeks 1–3, 5% weeks 4–6). No retroactive discounts beyond the 6-week window.
3) Service credit / liability cap: Service credits for any qualifying availability/latency incidents during the carveout are capped at 10% of that month's invoice. No changes to our broader indemnity or liability terms.
4) Performance gates: Mandatory joint review at week 3; if performance is not trending to p95 < 900ms by that checkpoint, extension requires Executive (VP-level) sign-off and finance approval.
4a) If Bluecrest introduces non-Redwood changes (client-side batching, proxy config), they must share release notes and test results 72 hours prior to deploy.
5) Documentation & signatures: Rishi, please prepare a 1-page amendment and a short runbook addendum. Camila, after Marissa's sign-off I'll send the amendment to Bluecrest for countersignature and begin the billing adjustments.

This approval is timeboxed: Camila may communicate the approved terms to Bluecrest and request confirmation. Any deviation (longer duration or higher discount) must come back to Execs.

Marissa Cole
Head of Deal Desk, Redwood Inference
